claims.text: The owner saw Olivier Laplace's LinkedIn post about the Harvard Business Review article he wrote with José Parra Moyano, Karl Schmedders and Benjamin Torben-Nielsen, and wanted to answer it.
claims.quote: the Harvard Business Review article he wrote with José Parra Moyano, Karl Schmedders and Benjamin Torben-Nielsen

claims.text: Simon Wardley's explorers, villagers and town planners explain the problem the HBR article describes, which is the owner's answer in Who will fix your mess.
claims.quote: I think Simon Wardley's explorers, villagers and town planners explain the problem it describes

claims.text: Clicking the link from LinkedIn gave a modal saying that reading HBR only on LinkedIn gets part of the story, then three subscription plans and no article.
claims.quote: If you only read HBR on Linkedin, you're only getting part of the story.

claims.text: HBR offered a UK reader Digital at £8.75 a month billed yearly or £11 monthly, Digital and Print at £10 or £13, and Premium at £15 or £18, every one a subscription.
claims.quote: Digital at £8.75 a month billed yearly, or £11 monthly.

value.unit: GBP a month for the digital plan

claims.text: The only other door is a reprint from HBR's store at $11.95, or $9.75 a copy for five to ten, a document priced for a team.
claims.quote: the article is sold as a reprint for $11.95, or $9.75 a copy if you buy five to ten

claims.text: The owner wants to pay HBR but not subscribe, because he knows how subscriptions end: paying for months not read, one article costing a hundred pounds.
claims.quote: I want to pay for it. I do not want to subscribe to it, because I know how subscriptions end

claims.text: HBR.org's own feed lists 45 articles published in September 2026, not counting podcasts, sponsored pieces or the magazine.
claims.quote: lists 45 articles published in September 2026, not counting podcasts, sponsored pieces or the magazine

value.unit: articles in HBR.org's feed for September 2026

claims.text: At £11 a month, reading all 45 is about 24p an article, twenty is about 55p, and ten is £1.10.
claims.quote: If I read every one of those 45, I am paying about 24p an article. If I read twenty, about 55p.

value.unit: pence an article at 45 a month

claims.text: The smallest thing a reader like the owner is allowed to buy is between ten and forty-five times bigger than what he wants, and that gap is the whole problem.
claims.quote: the smallest thing we are allowed to buy is between ten and forty-five times bigger than what we want

claims.text: On the newsroom every page has a price of a few pence, 10p for a new article and 5p for an older one, paid for the share read, after reading, from a balance in the browser.
claims.quote: 10p for a new article and 5p for an older one

value.unit: pence for a new article read to the end

claims.text: The newsroom has run with real payments since 11 October; the balance can go below zero, nothing is blocked, and the reader's rating sets what they pay from nothing to double.
claims.quote: At the foot of each article you say how useful it was, and that sets what you pay, from nothing to double.

claims.text: Ten things a reader would buy from one article, each a billable unit: eight run on the newsroom today and two are proposed.
claims.quote: Eight run on newsroom.sgit.ai today; two are proposed.

claims.text: A reading record of what was read and how much, with highlights, kept by the reader in an encrypted vault, and a persona for reading as a board member or security lead.
claims.quote: kept by me, not by the publisher

claims.text: The argument as a graph the reader can take into a company, and HBR's ontologies and taxonomies as a product kept in their own vocabulary.
claims.quote: Its ontologies and taxonomies, verified by its editors, are a product.

claims.text: The evidence as a graph of references the reader can follow, each step a page paid a little for, newer material costing more than the archive.
claims.quote: the references as a graph I can follow, where each step I take is a page I pay a little for

claims.text: A licence to quote with a share: the reader charges a little more for a page that answers HBR and passes it on, so the answer makes HBR money instead of competing with it.
claims.quote: I should be able to charge my readers a little more for that page and pass it on to HBR

claims.text: A check of use: an agent that checks a quote or an application of the article's advice was done correctly, worth paying for by the reader and by HBR.
claims.quote: an agent that checks I did it correctly would be worth paying for

claims.text: LinkedIn is not a leak but HBR's best market: the people discussing its articles there are the readers it wants.
claims.quote: I think it is HBR's best market.

claims.text: A post like Olivier's, with fifty reactions and twenty-one comments, is a room full of people HBR has no way to sell to.
claims.quote: A post like Olivier's, with fifty reactions and twenty-one comments, is a room full of people HBR has no way to sell to.

claims.text: Five things for HBR: sell the article after reading, sell what is behind it, license quotes and share in what they earn, let readers keep their reading, treat LinkedIn as a storefront.
claims.quote: Treat LinkedIn as a storefront.

claims.text: None of this needs inventing: it runs on newsroom.sgit.ai, and the reader's side is open source at api.newsroom.sgit.ai for any publisher to run.
claims.quote: the reader's side of it is open source at api.newsroom.sgit.ai, for any publisher to run on its own pages

claims.text: HBR's prices are as shown to a UK reader on 17 October 2026; other countries and offers will differ.
claims.quote: HBR's prices are as I saw them.

claims.text: The 45 is a lower bound, from HBR.org's feed without the magazine, podcasts or sponsored pieces.
claims.quote: The 45 is a lower bound.

claims.text: The newsroom's numbers are small; it shows the model works, not that it scales.
claims.quote: it shows the model works, not that it scales

claims.text: Two of the ten units, the licence to quote with a share and the check of use, are proposals not built here.
claims.quote: Two of the ten units are proposals.

claims.text: The owner has a stake: he builds the newsroom and its reader code and would like publishers to use it.
claims.quote: I build this newsroom and its reader code, and I would like publishers to use it.
